newsitem.title: BULGARIA: World Bank to lend Bulgaria $100 mln in September.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to lend Bulgaria $100 mln in September.

text.p: The World Bank is expected to approve a $100 million loan for Bulgaria in September as the country is fulfilling the bank's reform targets, a Bank official said on Friday.

"We will recommend to our management to approve the FESAL loan," said Frank Lysy, who is lead economist of the World Bank's Southeastern Europe department. FESAL stands for Financial Enterprise Sectoral Adjustment Loan.

Lysy told a news conference that a World Bank mission to Bulgaria which has just finished had been positive. It reviewed Bulgaria's progress in privatisation, closing loss-making state firms and the balance of payments.
The loan would be extended in early September because the procedure for approving it took three weeks and coincided with the World Bank board holiday, said Lysy.

The mission would also propose to the board that it should consider a second (FESAL) arrangement worth $70 million this calendar year if the new reformist government kept up the pace of structural reform, he added.

The bank has earmarked about $170 million in funding to Sofia under its FESAL programme out of a total $290 million package earmarked for Sofia this year. Three months ago the bank approved a first loan of $40 million for imports of essential goods such as grain, fuel and medical supplies.

Approval of a social safety net loan of $80 million to be targeted at the most vulnerable social groups such as pensioners, the unemployed and the disabled, is pending as the government progresses with closures of loss-makers.

Bulgaria stands to receive later this month a $130 million tranche from the International Monetary Fund, pledged to be disbursed once the country started a currency board system and deregulated trade in basic commodities.
Bulgaria introduced a fixed exchange rate regime on July 1 and has lifted most trade restrictions.
